description:
Byl's self-reproducing loop of twelve cells.

Source: J. Byl, "Self-reproduction in small cellular automata", Physica D 34
(1989) 295-299: Table II, the transition function for Fig. 3. As in the paper,
each transition is CTRBL->I (center, top, right, bottom and left, then the
center's next state), here the six digits C N E S W C'; rotations are not
listed (the rotate4 symmetry), and a group's default "C----", which applies
to any other neighborhood of that center, is the line with variables at the
end of the group.

Table II prints 56 entries, its defaults among them, where the paper's text
counts 57. With them alone, the run follows Fig. 3 until generation 22 and
then differs in one cell; the transition 31523 -> 1 makes every generation of
Fig. 3 come out, so it is added, marked, in its place among the 3s.

Fig. 3 is drawn as the mirror image (left and right swapped) of what Table II
gives under the paper's reading of the neighbors. The starter pattern
(Byl-Loop.rle) is therefore Fig. 3's loop mirrored, and its run is Fig. 3's,
mirrored: at generation 25 an exact copy of the loop of generation 0 stands
beside its parent.

Re-authored for heaton-life from the paper (spec/ruletable.md).
